{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Knight julia.jpg|thumb|Julia F. Knight, 2012]]
'''Julia Frandsen Knight''' is an American mathematician, specializing in [[model theory]] and [[computability theory]].<ref name="profile">[https://math.nd.edu/people/faculty/julia-knight/ Faculty profile], Notre Dame, retrieved 2013-10-16.</ref> She is the Charles L. Huisking Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Notre Dame]] and director of the graduate program in mathematics there.<ref name="huisking">[http://professorships.nd.edu/professorships/the-charles-l-huisking-professor-of-mathematics-1/ Julia Knight – Named professorships and directorships at Notre Dame] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017121320/http://professorships.nd.edu/professorships/the-charles-l-huisking-professor-of-mathematics-1/ |date=2013-10-17 }}, retrieved 2013-10-16.</ref>

== Education ==
Knight did her undergraduate studies at [[Utah State University]], graduating in 1964, and earned her Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1972 under the supervision of [[Robert Lawson Vaught]].<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=11628}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 2012, she became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of AMS Fellows], retrieved 2013-10-16.</ref> and she was elected to be the 30th president of the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]].<ref>[http://aslonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Jan2019newsletter.pdf ASL Newsletter, January 2019].</ref> She was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Simons Professor for Fall 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

In 2014, Knight held the [[Gödel Lecture]], titled ''Computable structure theory and formulas of special forms.''
